# Disagreement Log — Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 32

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Chapter:** SHE 032 — Mandate 4.2 (Post-Baptismal Repentance) — THE KEY CHAPTER
**Agents:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA

---

## Disagreements

### 1. V. 1 — "heard from some teachers" vs. "heard from certain teachers"
- **EMET:** "from some teachers"
- **LOGOS:** "from certain teachers"
- **PNEUMA:** "heard some teachers say"
- **Decision:** "from certain teachers" — tines = "certain ones"; LOGOS is precise

### 2. V. 3 — Scope of baptismal remission vs. post-baptismal repentance
- **EMET:** "have no repentance of sins; they have a remission of their former sins"
- **LOGOS:** "have no repentance for sins but only a remission of their former sins"
- **PNEUMA:** "don't get a second chance at repentance — they get a complete wiping clean"
- **Decision:** "have no repentance for sins; they have only a remission of their former sins" — the contrast between metanoia (repentance) and aphesis (remission/forgiveness) is theologically crucial and must be preserved precisely

### 3. V. 4 — "devices of the devil" vs. "tricks" vs. "wiles"
- **EMET:** "many wiles of the devil"
- **LOGOS:** "many devices of the devil"
- **PNEUMA:** "many tricks the devil had"
- **Decision:** "many devices of the devil" — methodeia = devices/stratagems; "wiles" is traditional but archaic

### 4. V. 6 — "sins and repents repeatedly" — the crucial phrase
- **EMET:** "sins and repents frequently"
- **LOGOS:** "sins and repents again and again"
- **PNEUMA:** "keeps sinning and keeps repenting, cycling through it over and over"
- **Decision:** "sins and keeps repenting repeatedly" — the key issue is the cyclical habit; "repeatedly" is clear and appropriate

### 5. V. 6 — "will with difficulty live to God" vs. "will find it nearly impossible to live to God"
- **EMET/LOGOS:** "will with difficulty live to God"
- **PNEUMA:** "will find it nearly impossible to live to God"
- **Decision:** "will with difficulty live to God" — mogis/chaleps = with difficulty; not "impossible" — the door remains theoretically open

### 6. V. 7 — "I received life when I heard" vs. "I have come alive in hearing"
- **EMET:** "I received life when I heard these things"
- **LOGOS:** "I have come alive in hearing"
- **PNEUMA:** "I feel like I've come alive just hearing this"
- **Decision:** "I have come alive in hearing these things" — the Greek ezōsan suggests a life-giving experience

**Total disagreements: 6**

### Theological Note for Council:
This chapter's "one repentance" teaching was enormously influential. The three agents' handling differs in important ways:
- EMET preserves the technical terminology most precisely
- LOGOS provides the clearest theological framework
- PNEUMA makes the pastoral implications most vivid but risks oversimplifying

SOPHIA synthesizes all three while ensuring the crucial distinction between remission (at baptism) and post-baptismal repentance (once only) is preserved.
